channel.title: Megajournal Feed
channel.description: Aggregated research articles from the multidisciplinary megajournals: Nature Communications, restricted to biological and health sciences, and Science Advances, which is not filtered by subject because no accessible source exposes one.

item.title: Nature Communications: UpTCR: a unified progressive knowledge transfer foundation model for robust T-cell receptor-antigen binding recognition
item.description: Peptides are presented to T Cell receptors (TCR) in the context of human leukocyte antigen (HLA) MHC molecules and the prediction of these peptide sequences are important for vaccines and cancer therapeutics. Here the authors present UpTCR a computational method for learning from incomplete data for TCR-antigen-HLA prediction, considering antigen-HLA binding affinity and specificity and using this tool to predict epitopes in breast cancer patient cohorts.

item.title: Nature Communications: Long-read RNA sequencing identifies non-coding isoform switching as a regulator of cell fate
item.description: Exploration of the functional relevance of isoform diversity during cell fate regulation is limited. Here, the authors leverage long-read RNA sequencing during somatic cell reprogramming to demonstrate that isoform switching plays a previously overlooked functional role in cell fate changes.

item.title: Nature Communications: Stepwise pairing and fast transition regulated by recombination drive meiotic chromosome interactions
item.description: Chromosomes must pair accurately to form healthy reproductive cells. Here, the authors show in mice that this pairing occurs in defined steps controlled by DNA recombination and chromosome-joining structures.

item.title: Nature Communications: Spatiotemporal delivery of immune-synapse-stabilizing NK cells for postoperative tumor therapy
item.description: Here, Li and colleagues report that arming NK cells with surface-anchored, multivalent galectin-3 binding polymers prolongs NK-to-tumor target cell contact and enhances NK cytotoxicity; as well, authors describe that a semi-spike patch for spatiotemporal delivery of armed NK cells in the resection cavity prevents tumor recurrence post-surgery.

item.title: Nature Communications: ARHGEF2 isoform switching couples intestinal epithelial barrier function with autophagic host defense response to pathogens
item.description: Different forms of GEF-H1 coordinate the gut’s defenses: long forms build and maintain the intestinal barrier, while barrier damage triggers a short form that helps cells capture and destroy invading bacteria such as Listeria .

item.title: Nature Communications: DR-GEM enables self-supervised machine learning for single-cell embeddings and annotations
item.description: Here the authors show that current dimensionality reduction methods for single-cell and spatial genomics data often favor abundant patterns and overlook rare ones. They develop DR-GEM, a self-supervised framework that diagnoses and learns from its errors to recover underrepresented biological signals.

item.title: Nature Communications: A global S-palmitoylation map of Trypanosoma cruzi identifies ABCA10 as a key component of a redundant heme-acquisition system
item.description: The Chagas disease parasite, T. cruzi, cannot make heme, and so must steal it to survive. Researchers mapping its fatty-acid-tagged proteins identified ABCA10, an ABC transporter at the core of this heme-scavenging system and a promising new drug target.

item.title: Nature Communications: Systematic comparison of phenome-wide admixture mapping and genome-wide association at biobank-scale
item.description: Cullina et al. apply admixture mapping and GWAS at phenome-wide scale in Hispanic/Latino and African American participants, showing that systematic comparison of both methods uncovers complementary disease associations in admixed populations.

item.title: Nature Communications: Navigational strategy dictates hippocampal representation of space in an everyday memory task
item.description: Neurobiology of spatial memory is not fully understood. Using two behavioral tasks, authors demonstrate that the precision of spatial representations is lower in rats using egocentric coordinates, and hippocampus silencing correct only affects goal identification in rats performing allocentrically.

item.title: Nature Communications: Identification of substrates of the human mitochondrial ClpXP protease and its implications for Perrault syndrome
item.description: The ClpXP ATP-dependent unfoldase-protease complex plays important roles in maintaining protein homeostasis in the mitochondria. Here, the authors identify three substrates of ClpXP that are dysregulated in PRLTS3 patients and show that degradation of these substrates requires the adaptor PDIP38.

item.title: Nature Communications: High-throughput label-free single-cell proteomics enabled by multicolumn NanoLC
item.description: Single-cell proteomics reveals cellular diversity, but the throughput has been limited. Here, the authors develop a high-throughput multicolumn nanoLC system that analyzes up to 288 cells per day, identifies ~ 4,000 proteins per cell and profiles inflammatory responses in macrophages.

item.title: Nature Communications: SATB1 lowers the T cell receptor signaling threshold for thymocyte positive selection via super-enhancer reprogramming
item.description: Satb1 is a chromatin organizer involved in T cell development. Here, the authors demonstrate that Satb1 reorganizes super-enhancer topology to promote the expression of genes associated with thymic positive selection.

item.title: Nature Communications: The Neural Mechanism of Motion Sickness Alleviation by Anticipatory Sound
item.description: The neural basis of motion sickness is not fully understood. Here, the authors show that anticipatory sound reduces motion sickness-like responses in mice by activating an inhibitory brain pathway that dampens balance-processing neurons and separates movement symptoms from nausea-related aversion.

item.title: Nature Communications: Entrainment of prefrontal theta synchrony increases interbrain coupling and enhances social interaction in mouse models of autism
item.description: Brain rhythms of interacting mice become synchronized, but this coordination is reduced in mouse models of autism. Here the authors show that theta-frequency stimulation is accompanied by increased interbrain synchrony and social interaction.

item.title: Nature Communications: Extended dosing intervals enhance the durability of a self-amplifying mRNA vaccine against pandemic H5N1 influenza: a randomized, observer-blind, dose-finding Phase I study
item.description: Here, the authors present a Phase 1 randomized, observer-blind trial of ARCT-2304, a bicistronic self-amplifying mRNA vaccine against H5N1 influenza. The findings support a potential role for self-amplifying mRNA platforms against influenza.

item.title: Nature Communications: Abrupt pH changes overestimate the responses of Chaetoceros muelleri to ocean acidification
item.description: Ocean acidification influences diatom carbon fixation, yet most experiments use abrupt pH shifts. This study’s 1100-generation experiment finds that abrupt pH reduction overestimates Chaetoceros muelleri responses to ocean acidification at the physiological, transcriptomic, and genomic levels.

item.title: Nature Communications: Reoviridae -derived short trimerization domain for stabilizing homo-trimerization of vaccine immunogens and therapeutic proteins
item.description: In this study, the authors engineer a short trimerization tag for vaccine and therapeutic protein development. The tag enables a trimeric ACE2 decoy that exhibits broad neutralizing activity against coronaviruses and confers protection in animal models.

item.title: Nature Communications: Surface-displayed cholesterol enhances penetration and anti-tumor activity of a platinum nanodrug by targeting NPC1L1-expressing cancer associated fibroblasts
item.description: Cancer associated fibroblasts can represent a physical barrier for drug delivery in tumor cells. Here the authors show that, by selectively targeting NPC1L1-cancer associated fibroblasts, surface-displayed cholesterol enhances the delivery of a platinum nanodrug in stroma-rich tumors, restoring anti-tumor efficacy.

item.title: Nature Communications: Multimodal hydrogel modulation of extracellular vesicle cargo to arrest post-traumatic osteoarthritis in murine models
item.description: Here, the authors develop a mechano-responsive lubricating hydrogel that releases bioactive molecules under joint stress to interrupt the inflammatory cycle is osteoarthritis. In rat models, it prevents cartilage damage and restores motor function within eight weeks, offering a potential strategy for early osteoarthritis intervention.

item.title: Nature Communications: Ligand-induced activation of RyR1 in native membranes
item.description: Effective muscle contraction relies on synchronized opening of RyR1 calcium channels. Here, authors present high-resolution structures of RyR1 in native membranes, revealing how ligand-induced activation of receptors leads to synchronous activation.

item.title: Nature Communications: Shield strike shatter in DNA topology and nuclease interactions
item.description: Researchers visualize how DNA topology governs nuclease interactions in real time. High-speed atomic force microscopy reveals dynamic enzyme scanning, DNA protection by protamine condensation, and topology-dependent cleavage, uncovering nanoscale principles of genome accessibility.

item.title: Nature Communications: Spatiotemporal characterization of Alzheimer disease pathology in living human brain tissue
item.description: This study uses brain biopsies collected during shunt surgery to examine early Alzheimer disease in living brain tissue, showing rapid tau turnover and stable amyloid plaques.

item.title: Nature Communications: Chronic stress activates a hypothalamic vagal circuit to promote hepatocellular carcinoma progression in male mice
item.description: Chronic stress can promote hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) progression. Here, the authors show in mice that chronic stress activates a brain-liver signaling circuit that mediates tumor epithelial-macrophage crosstalk and promotes HCC growth.

Science Advances: Pacific tsunami records suggest similar rupture locations of two great Kamchatka earthquakes only 73 years apart
