Nature Communications: Hydrogen sulfide engages catalytic zinc in HDAC6 to modulate an alternative deacetylation pathway
item.description: Hydrogen sulfide is a gasotransmitter whose non-covalent effects on protein function remain incompletely understood. Here the authors show that hydrogen sulfide interacts with zinc in the enzyme HDAC6, changes how it removes acetyl groups from proteins, and contributes to blood-vessel growth.

item.title: Nature Communications: Calcium induced N-terminal gating and pore collapse in connexin-46/50 gap junctions
item.description: Gap junctions establish direct communication pathways between neighboring cells that are shut down during cellular stress. Here, authors show how calcium reshapes connexin channels to promote N terminal pore closure through a dynamic ensemble of gated state.

item.title: Nature Communications: Elevated ozone activates maternal immunity to drive offspring IgG-mediated anaphylaxis through IgG glycosylation alterations
item.description: Environmental pollution may have effects upon unborn children. Here the authors look at human retrospective data and use mouse models to show that ozone exposure during pregnancy can promote allergy susceptibility in adult offspring and this may involve changes in IgG glycosylation and increased inflammation.

item.title: Nature Communications: Loss of intestinal Akt elicits rapid mortality via intestinal damage which is rescued by mTORC1 activation
item.description: Akt is required for intestinal integrity, and Akt1/Akt2 intestinal deletion induces rapid mortality in mice, which is recapitulated by pan-PI3K and Akt inhibitors, and is reversed by activating mTORC1 via additional deletion of either FoxO1 or Tsc1.

item.title: Nature Communications: Inducible chronic NAD deficiency in mice reveals multi-systemic phenotypical, metabolic, and transcriptional changes
item.description: The authors show that chronic NAD deficiency causes widespread metabolic, physical, and cellular changes, including senescence and inflammation, while dietary niacin restores NAD levels and reverses most of these effects.

item.title: Nature Communications: A spatiotemporal single-cell transcriptomic atlas reveals fertilization-induced auxin signaling driving strawberry fruit set and development
item.description: Fertilization-triggered fruit set and morphogenesis is a complex process involving multiple cell types. Here the authors use spatial transcriptomics and single nucleus RNA-seq to map fertilization induced changes in woodland strawberry.

item.title: Nature Communications: The elongation of Mest transcript into MestXL sustains, but does not initiate, the maternal allele bias of its convergent gene Copg2 during neurogenesis
item.description: Precise dosage control of imprinted genes is essential for neurodevelopment, but the mechanisms regulating allele-specific expression remain incompletely understood. Here, the authors show that maternally biased Copg2 expression arises through a two-step mechanism involving enhancer-mediated maternal activation followed by MestXL-dependent repression of the paternal allele.

item.title: Nature Communications: CPT1A-mediated IDO1 succinylation shapes EGFRvIII-driven resistance to tumor electric field therapy in glioblastoma
item.description: Tumour electric field therapy (TEFT) can improve survival in glioblastoma, but responses vary. Here, the authors show that EGFRvIII turns TEFT-induced bioenergetic stress into cytoskeletal protection via IDO1 upregulation and CPT1A-mediated IDO1 stabilisation which can be therapeutically targeted with EGFR inhibition.

item.title: Nature Communications: Ghost Neuron preparation unlocks high-resolution structural mapping of intracellular architecture in axons
item.description: The authors introduce Ghost Neuron, a cryo-EM preparation that improves visualization of neuronal projections and maps macromolecular structures within axons at near-atomic resolution.

item.title: Nature Communications: The biogeography of giant viruses and interactions with Eukaryotes across European lakes
item.description: Large and giant DNA viruses are widespread in nature but their ecology remains poorly understood in freshwater ecosystems. This study finds that giant viruses are abundant in warmer waters where they are linked to lower primary production.

item.title: Nature Communications: Gα12/13 deficiency attenuates obesity-associated adipose tissue inflammation and promotes energy expenditure
item.description: Obesity impairs adipose function and drives metabolic disease. Here, the authors show that obesity-induced Gα12/13 restrains β-adrenergic signaling; its loss raises energy expenditure and protects mice from diet-induced metabolic dysfunction.

item.title: Nature Communications: A principal-stress rule for cell division in epithelia
item.description: The search for general physical principles that govern biological organization has long motivated studies of tissue mechanics. In this work, the authors show that a simple mechanical rule based on principal stress predicts the orientation and rate of cell division across dense epithelial systems, revealing cell division as a key mechanism for stress regulation in living matter.

item.title: Nature Communications: Neoadjuvant chemotherapy interferes with tertiary lymphoid structure formation in Epstein-Barr virus-associated gastric cancer
item.description: Efficacy of neoadjuvant chemotherapy (NAC) in patients with EBV-associated gastric cancer (EBVaGC) remains controversial. Here the authors show that, by promoting EBV reactivation and neutrophil extracellular trap formation, NAC disrupts tertiary lymphoid structure formation in patients with EBVaGC.

item.title: Nature Communications: Systemic and Mucosal Antibody Responses Against Neisseria gonorrhoeae ( Ng ) Outer Membrane Vesicle Antigens following Four-Component Meningococcal Serogroup B (4CMenB) Immunization in Healthy Adults: A Randomized Phase II Trial
item.description: This phase 2, double-blind, randomized, placebo-controlled trial shows that a two-dose series of 4CMenB vaccine induces both systemic and mucosal IgG responses to Neisseria gonorrhoeae, suggesting a potential role in gonorrhea prevention.

item.title: Nature Communications: Canonical Notch2 signaling regulates development and maintenance of iron-recycling macrophages and iron homeostasis
item.description: Red pulp and bone marrow macrophages play roles in iron homeostasis and erythropoiesis via molecular pathways not fully known. Here the authors show, via conditional deletion approaches in monocyte/macrophage progenitors in mice, that canonical Notch2 signalling is necessary for the development and function of iron-recycling macrophages.

item.title: Nature Communications: Structural basis of step II spliced leader RNA trans-splicing in trypanosomatid parasites
item.description: Trypanosomatid parasites rely on Spliced Leader (SL) RNA trans-splicing to produce every mature mRNA. Here, the authors present cryo-EM structures of the trans spliceosome during SL exon ligation, providing structural insight into this essential RNA processing pathway.

item.title: Nature Communications: Single-cell mapping of chromosome breaks identifies multiple fragile site classes with distinct DNA replication timing landscapes
item.description: Common Fragile Sites are genomic regions prone to breakage. However, other fragile sites remain underexplored. Here, the authors used single-cell genomics to map replication stress-induced breaks, identifying multiple fragile site classes with distinct features and DNA replication timing landscapes.

item.title: Nature Communications: Payoff selectivity drives collective intelligence during dynamic resource tracking in humans
item.description: Humans rely on complex social learning and collective adaptation to navigate dynamically changing environments. The authors show that human collective intelligence in a dynamic, naturalistic task depends on access to payoff information.

item.title: Nature Communications: Fast, flexible analysis of differences in cellular composition with crumblr
item.description: Statistical analysis of single-cell compositional data can be challenging. Here, Hoffman and Roussos develop the crumblr method and software to identify differences in cellular composition in single-cell datasets by incorporating the cell lineage hierarchy.

item.title: Nature Communications: Personalized single-cell transcriptomics reveals molecular diversity in Alzheimer’s disease
item.description: Personalized functional genomics atlas for Alzheimer’s disease that uses knowledge-guided graph neural networks to analyze donor-level functional genomics, identify disease subpopulations and trajectories, and link genetic variants to gene regulation.

item.title: Nature Communications: Efficient differential expression analysis of large-scale single-cell transcriptomics data using Dreamlet
item.description: Single cell transcriptomics have enabled generation of increasingly large-scale datasets from hundreds of subjects and millions of cells. Here, authors develop the dreamlet package for efficient differential expression analysis of large-scale single cell datasets.

item.title: Nature Communications: Cross-talk of filter gate and lower helices drives polymodal regulation and disease in TREK channels
item.description: Here the authors perform advanced simulations and experiments to reveal how coordinated structural changes regulate TREK-2 potassium channel activity and how disease-associated mutations disrupt this mechanism, providing atomistic insights into neurological disorders.

item.title: Nature Communications: Unveiling structural determinants of peptide recognition by public and private SARS-CoV-2-specific T-cell receptors
item.description: Public TCR receptors are shared across individuals, but private TCRs are more restricted. Here the authors look at the biophysical differences between a public and a private TCR that recognise an HLA-A*01:01 restricted SARS-CoV-2 ORF3a epitope and show divergent alpha chains, differing engagement of CDR-loop configurations and contact footprints.

item.title: Nature Communications: EpOME functionally antagonises prostaglandin signalling in Spodoptera exigua via a specific GPCR conserved across metazoans
item.description: Prostaglandin signalling is a conserved feature in metazoan immunity, however, the regulatory mechanisms in insects are not fully known. Here the authors identify a phylogenetically conserved GPCR in the insect Spodoptera exigua that delivers inhibitory signals to prostaglandin-mediated immunity via binding the ligand EpOME.

item.title: Nature Communications: Structure and functional divergence of the non-canonical BoNT-like toxin PG1 and PG2
item.description: Here the authors characterise two botulinum-like toxins, PG1 and PG2. Their light chains cut a key protein in fruit flies; PG1 is toxic even without its heavy chain. PG1 has a distinct compact structure. These findings expand toxin knowledge and suggest potential as insecticides or research tools.

item.title: Nature Communications: Structural basis of laminin mimicry by E. coli CNF1 and its therapeutic potential for cancer immunotherapy
item.description: The authors show how the bacterial toxin CNF1 mimics laminin to hijack its cell-surface receptor BCAM, and how this interaction can be repurposed to guide T cells to selectively kill BCAM-expressing cancer cells.

item.title: Nature Communications: Short-term memory of past caspase activity biases cell elimination in vivo
item.description: Quantitative live imaging, machine learning and optogenetics in the Drosophila pupal thorax epithelium reveal the influence of past exposure to sublethal caspase activation, which sensitises cells for apoptosis for several hours and can bias cell elimination.

item.title: Nature Communications: Actionable genetic landscape and dynamics in circulating DNA from 12,827 patients with metastatic breast cancer
item.description: Metastatic breast cancer remains a heterogenous disease which is difficult to treat effectively. Here, the authors survey over 15,000 samples via cfDNA analysis and characterize the landscape of targetable alterations across major breast cancer subtypes.

item.title: Nature Communications: Patient-derived separation-of-function mutations reveal specific role for BRCA1 coiled coil domain in genome stability
item.description: Inherited mutations of BRCA1 can compromise homologous recombination repair and increase cancer risk. Here, the authors show that such mutations differentially impact genome instability in cultured cells, suggesting a specific role for the BRCA1-PALB2 interaction in error-free DNA damage bypass.

item.title: Nature Communications: p38α orchestrates BRAF V600E -melanoma progression and immunotherapy response via tumor fitness and immune microenvironment modulation
item.description: The role of p38 activation in melanoma remains controversial. Here the authors report that, in an UVB induced Braf V600E -mutated spontaneous mouse melanoma model, p38α contributes to tumor fitness and anti-tumor immune responses, showing that p38α inhibition sensitizes tumors to anti-PD1.

item.title: Nature Communications: Single-cell TimeLapse-seq reveals MTA is an essential retrotransposon orchestrating mouse zygotic genome activation
item.description: This study establishes scTimeLapse-seq to redefine mouse ZGA into three transcriptional waves. It unveils MTA-MaLR as the earliest activated retrotransposon, which acts as a key regulator of ZGA initiation and early embryonic development.

item.title: Nature Communications: Attractin-like protein 1 is an essential partner of MC4R to regulate body weight
item.description: The authors identified ATRNL1 as a key regulator of MC4R for appetite control. Loss of ATRNL1 or damaging ATRNL1 variants result in impaired MC4R signaling, increased food intake and promote weight gain. Mutations in Atrnl1 could contribute to obesity.

item.title: Nature Communications: Microglial protein kinase CK2 prevents obesity in mice potentially through NLRP3 inflammasome activation
item.description: The study demonstrates that microglial protein kinase CK2 prevents obesity in part via regulating food intake, potentially by regulating IL-18 production through ASC phosphorylation mediated NLRP3 inflammasome activation.

item.title: Nature Communications: Resilience of blue carbon microbiomes in response to ecological and anthropogenic filtering
item.description: Blue carbon ecosystems provide vital services underpinned by microbial communities, yet their responses to environmental change are unclear. This study uses metagenomics to reveal stable microbial functions despite taxonomic turnover.

item.title: Nature Communications: Oropouche virus disrupts neurodevelopment and exhibits congenital infection potential
item.description: Bannerman et al. demonstrate that OROV causes severe neurodevelopmental pathology in human brain models and has the potential for congenital infection in murine models.

item.title: Nature Communications: Histone deacetylase inhibition induces an antitumor IRF8-dependent trained immunity-like status in macrophages
item.description: Induction of trained immunity can elicit anti-tumor effects. Here the authors show that histone deacetylase inhibitor preconditioning elicits a IRF8-dependent trained immunity-like status in monocytes/macrophages, promoting anti-tumor immunity in multiple triple negative breast cancer models.

item.title: Nature Communications: Extensive horizontal gene transfer drives microbial adaptation and diversification in Kermadec Trench hadal microbiomes
item.description: This study uses metagenomics and in situ metatranscriptomics to explore microbial ecology from deep sea hadal trenches. They find that viruses and magnetotactic bacteria possibly help distant phyla share functional genes to survive extreme pressure and starvation.

item.title: Nature Communications: Long-range interdependencies aware signal analysis for rapid and accurate obstructive sleep apnea prediction
item.description: Researchers develop a framework that captures long-range physiological interactions from sleep recordings to predict obstructive sleep apnea severity. Validated in more than 35,000 individuals, it shows robust performance across diverse populations.

item.title: Nature Communications: Generative AI designs functional thiolation domains for reprogramming non-ribosomal peptide synthetases
item.description: AI has designed protein domains that nature never made. Here, the authors apply generative models to bacterial enzymatic assembly lines that build antibiotics; the best de novo thiolation domain designs beat the natural part they replace — tripling output and keeping hybrid enzymes active.

item.title: Nature Communications: Structural basis of lenacapavir-induced HIV-1 capsid defects during virion maturation
item.description: Long-acting lenacapavir is a HIV-1 capsid inhibitor. Here the authors reveal that lenacapavir alters capsid lattice curvature during virion maturation, preventing formation of a functional cone-shaped capsid.

item.title: Nature Communications: A Hadean timeline for the emergence of the RNA World
item.description: A 3-D thermal model identifies a ~ 4.33 Ga temporal “sweet spot” for life’s origin, when decreased bombardment enabled mild hydrothermal niches to support RNA World chemistry and stable biomolecule preservation, congruent with LUCA estimates.

item.title: Nature Communications: Host-pathogen pyrimidine metabolism drives cystic fibrosis lung disease
item.description: Here, Lohia et al show that pyrimidine metabolism is a driver of pulmonary remodelling and bacterial infection in people with cystic fibrosis.

item.title: Nature Communications: Risk stratification for MDR/RR-TB: a comprehensive integrated patient-level analysis from TB programs and contemporary clinical trials
item.description: Pooling data from 7750 patients with drug-resistant tuberculosis worldwide, in this study, the authors defined disease-severity phenotypes based on clinical and treatment features, stratifying patients by risk of unfavourable outcomes to enable risk-adapted, stratified care.

item.title: Nature Communications: Mortality and healthcare services in Pennsylvania state prisons following extreme ambient temperatures
item.description: Extreme hot and cold temperatures are determinants of mortality for incarcerated populations and this manuscript shows that temperature extremes increase demand on already strained prison healthcare systems.

item.title: Nature Communications: Carbon nanotubes as the supporting film for cryo-EM specimen preparation
item.description: Cryo-EM specimen preparation is often hindered by air–water interface. Here, authors develop carbon nanotube supports that protect macromolecules and enable affinity purification, providing a versatile platform for structural studies.

item.title: Nature Communications: Structure of Blm10:13S proteasome intermediate reveals parallel assembly pathways for the proteasome core particle
item.description: Proteasomes can be capped by regulatory particles other than the 19S complex, but how these form is unclear. Here, authors reveal cryo-EM structures of Blm10-proteasome assembly intermediates and provide evidence for parallel assembly pathways.

item.title: Nature Communications: Live imaging and interactome analysis of Zika and chikungunya viral RNAs via dual-action aptamer tag
item.description: The study describes the implementation of an RNA tag that enables visualization of Zika and chikungunya virus genomes in live cells and identifies critical host proteins that interact with the genomes for these viruses to replicate efficiently.

item.title: Nature Communications: Genetic variants associated with cell-type-specific intra-individual gene expression variability reveal mechanisms of genome regulation
item.description: Using over 1.2 million single immune cells, the authors identify genetic variants that influence cell-to-cell variation in gene expression, revealing a previously hidden layer of genome regulation associated with immune function and autoimmune disease.

item.title: Nature Communications: Single-oocyte proteome-transcriptome co-profiling reveals a role of dysregulated lactate metabolism in oocyte aging
item.description: Age-related deterioration in oocyte quality is a key contributor to female infertility. Here, Cao et al. co-profile RNA and proteins in single mouse and human oocytes, revealing the molecular landscape and heterogeneity of oocyte aging and identifying MCT4-mediated lactate export as a potential marker and intervention target.

item.title: Nature Communications: Integrative structure of norovirus NS3 suggests a role in RNA transport
item.description: Norovirus is the leading global cause of acute gastroenteritis. Here, the authors elucidate norovirus replication and show that the viral NS3 protein forms an RNA-engaging molecular motor that may transport viral RNA during infection.

item.title: Nature Communications: A phage DUF669 protein mediates post-cleavage DNA repair against host CRISPR immunity
item.description: Using affinity purification-mass spectrometry, these authors identified the Healer system, a phage two-protein effector that repairs CRISPR-mediated DNA breaks via homologous recombination.

item.title: Nature Communications: Generating protein hydrogels with customizable stress relaxation behavior via deep learning-driven entanglement design
item.description: Stress relaxation is increasingly recognized as a critical property of protein hydrogels for tissue engineering. To expand the limited toolbox of inter-chain entangled motifs, the authors develop an integrated workflow combining data mining, generative AI, virtual screening, and experimentation. The platform enables the design of entangled proteins and the fabrication of seven hydrogels with tailored stress relaxation profiles, demonstrating a direct correlation between predicted binding energies and material performance.

item.title: Nature Communications: Post-2020 conservation priorities are threatened by global mining
item.description: Mining threatens biodiversity worldwide, yet its full impact remains unclear. Here, authors reveal that extensive current and future mining areas overlap with conservation priority zones and threatened species.

item.title: Nature Communications: Multichannel, biomimetic scaffolds improve functional connectivity following traumatic long-gap peripheral nerve injury
item.description: Peripheral nerve injuries are typically repaired using nerve autografts despite donor-site morbidity. Here, the authors show that a biomimetic multichannel scaffold that organizes axonal regeneration, matches or surpasses autografts performance in preclinical models.

item.title: Nature Communications: RIPK3 acts as a molecular switch between neuroprotection and neuropathology during herpes simplex encephalitis
item.description: HSV-1 encephalitis causes severe brain injury, but the mechanism of immune pathology remains to be explored. The authors here show that RIPK3 drives astrocyte death though benefits viral control in other cell types, further RIPK3 inhibition promotes survival.

item.title: Nature Communications: Five-country analysis of geographic and dietary drivers of gut microbiome composition and genomic variation
item.description: In this study, authors show that human gut microbiome composition and microbial genomes vary strongly across five industrialized countries, with diet microbiome links that are partly shared but largely population-specific.

item.title: Nature Communications: Combinatorial targeting of the miR-379/miR-410 cluster normalizes glucose and lipid homeostasis in male models of diabetes and obesity
item.description: Hepatic-specific repression of the miR-379/miR-410 cluster in adult mice impacts hepatic insulin signalling and affects whole-body glucose and lipid metabolism, improving glycemic control and dyslipidemia in male models of obesity and diabetes.

item.title: Nature Communications: PUM3 is an essential suppressor of replication stress in homologous recombination deficient breast cancer
item.description: How tumour cells survive defective homologous recombination (HR) DNA repair has not been fully understood. Here the authors find that PUM3 prevents transcription replication conflicts and accumulation of R-loops through recruiting the DNA topoisomerase TOP1 in HR-defective triple negative breast cancer cells.

item.title: Nature Communications: Combinatorial mechanisms specify cellular location and neurotransmitter identity during planarian neurogenesis
item.description: During regeneration, new neurons need to be made in a way that reproduces both neuronal diversity and organization. Here the authors show that a combination of factors works cooperatively to direct neuron type and place in brain regeneration in planarians.

item.title: Nature Communications: Scalable molecular representations enabled by multimodal fusion and sequence distillation
item.description: This study integrates six complementary molecular representations into a distilled molecular string embedding, enabling scalable property prediction and prioritization of compounds that reduce DNA-damage phenotypes in yeast.

item.title: Nature Communications: Extending single-cell proteomics from HeLa to small primary human immune cells
item.description: Single-cell proteomics can reveal cellular heterogeneity but remains challenging for small cells. Here, the authors establish a sensitive label-free workflow that quantifies up to 7,000 proteins per HeLa cell and up to 4,000 proteins in small human immune cells.

item.title: Nature Communications: Dosing and delivery of bacteriophage therapy in a murine wound infection model
item.description: Here, the authors develop a mouse model of wound infection to evaluate the efficacy of phage therapy for established infections and generate “HydroPhage”, a phage-containing hydrogel, as a means for sustained delivery and topical phage application.

item.title: Nature Communications: Spatial partitioning of NSD2 defines H3K36me2 as an active mark for repetitive sequence activation
item.description: The authors reveal how TOP1 and MTA1 direct the epigenetic enzyme NSD2 to different genomic regions, placing H3K36me2 on gene bodies to support transcription and on repetitive sequences to activate their expression.

item.title: Nature Communications: Cryo-EM structure of ex vivo Sup35 yeast prion and the factors defining prion phenotype
item.description: Here, authors present the cryo-EM structure of a “strong” Sup35 prion purified from yeast, comprising residues 2–64. This structure differs significantly from that of Sup35 amyloid generated in vitro at 4˚C, but fits earlier proteinase K mapping data.

item.title: Nature Communications: Disruption of SWI/SNF ATPases in the mouse liver impairs diurnal gene expression associated with specific promoter features
item.description: SWI/SNF chromatin remodeling maintains cis-regulatory accessibility in the liver, enabling diurnal gene expression and supporting liver homeostasis during daily fasting-to-feeding transitions.

item.title: Nature Communications: The EF1α promoter of cilta-cel drives a highly effective GZMK + transcriptional program
item.description: Chimaeric antigen receptors (CAR) approved for the treatment of multiple myeloma have been reported to have different therapeutic efficacies. In this study, the authors demonstrate that this difference stems from promoter choice, rather than the antigen-binding domain of the CAR.

item.title: Nature Communications: Bayesian bilevel operator learning with low-rank adaptation for efficient uncertainty quantification of PDE inverse problems
item.description: Estimating parameters of partial differential equations from data with quantified uncertainty is computationally demanding. Here, authors combine bilevel local operator learning with low rank adaptation to enable efficient gradient-based posterior sampling without adjoint equations, pretraining data, or sampling network weights.

item.title: Nature Communications: Anti-thymocyte globulin triggers TNF-dependent cell death in T-cell acute lymphoblastic leukemia
item.description: Anti-thymocyte globulin (ATG) is a potent immunosuppressant used to prevent and treat acute organ transplant rejection and severe aplastic anemia. Here, the authors discover that ATG can be repurposed to induce TNF-driven cell death in T cell acute lymphoblastic leukemia.

item.title: Nature Communications: Learning chemical-induced gene expression perturbations with WAVE
item.description: Drug-induced gene expression profiles can reveal compound mechanisms but are difficult to generate at scale. Here, the authors present WAVE, a deep learning model that accurately predicts bulk and single-cell drug responses, with experimental validation supporting its potential for drug discovery.

item.title: Nature Communications: Characterization of recombinase-based genetic parts and circuits using nanopore sequencing
item.description: Measuring the accuracy of recombinase activity is often laborious, time-consuming, and costly. Here, the authors develop a semi-automated workflow that enables the high-throughput characterization of recombinase parts and circuits in a variety of contexts and organisms.

item.title: Nature Communications: Imaging nanoscopic co-assemblies of α-synuclein and Tau in human samples
item.description: Here the authors employ an optimised single-molecule pull-down (SiMPull) to investigate nanoscopic αS, Tau, and Aβ-containing assemblies in human brain tissue and biofluids. They establish a framework for detecting and comparing nanoscopic co-assemblies.

item.title: Nature Communications: Uncoupling of the allosteric signalling network in the β 1 -adrenergic receptor by a negative allosteric modulator
item.description: Understanding allosteric modulation mechanisms at G protein-coupled receptors (GPCRs) is key to development of therapeutics. Here, the authors show how a negative allosteric modulator acts to uncouple the signalling network of β1-adrenergic receptor.

item.title: Nature Communications: BEAR-GRN: Systematic assessment of single-cell multi-omics-based gene regulatory network inference methods
item.description: BEAR-GRN provides a standardized framework for benchmarking gene regulatory network inference methods using single-cell multi-omics data, revealing that ground-truth choice profoundly impacts performance and that current methods remain predominantly RNA-driven.

item.title: Nature Communications: Cell-type-specific surfaceome profiling of 100-500 isolated cells using a droplet-based Magnetic Affinity Purification System
item.description: Surface proteins are a key source of biomarkers and therapeutic targets, but remain poorly characterized in disease-relevant cells. Here, authors developed nanoMAPS, an ultrasensitive proteomic method to profile surface proteins from hundreds of primary cells and identify potential biomarkers.

item.title: Nature Communications: The DNMT1 CXXC domain senses CpG islands for DNA methylation inhibition
item.description: DNA methylation patterns must be maintained while protecting CpG islands from inappropriate methylation. Here, the authors show that the DNMT1 CXXC domain binds unmethylated CpG sites on nucleosomes to block DNMT1 activity, thereby safeguarding CpG island hypomethylation and normal stem cell differentiation.

item.title: Nature Communications: A temporal single cell atlas of dynamic chromatin accessibility during murine lung maturation
item.description: Lung maturation involves dynamic epigenetic remodelling that is not fully understood. Here, the authors develop an ultra-high-throughput single-cell ATAC-seq method and generate a temporal atlas of 1.2 million lung nuclei, revealing regulatory programs that shape postnatal lung development and disease risk.

item.title: Nature Communications: Small extracellular vesicle-mediated epithelial–macrophage crosstalk contributes to macrophage dysfunction during PEDV infection
item.description: Here, Li and colleagues show that porcine epidemic diarrhea virus alters the RNA cargo of small extracellular vesicles from intestinal epithelial cells. These vesicles weaken intestinal immune defence by impairing macrophage migration and phagocytosis.

item.title: Nature Communications: ReScale4DL: balancing pixel and contextual information for enhanced bioimage segmentation
item.description: Deep-learning segmentation accuracy depends on image resolution, with each architecture having an optimum, usually at a lower microscopy resolution. Here, the authors present ReScale4DL, a framework for optimising imaging experiments by selecting resolutions to balance accuracy, throughput and cost.

item.title: Nature Communications: Microglia and border-associated macrophages play opposite roles in cerebrovascular and leukocyte responses under systemic inflammation in male mice
item.description: How brain myeloid cells regulate vascular responses in systemic inflammation is unclear. Here, the authors identify distinct roles for microglia and border-associated macrophages in leukocyte recruitment and cerebral blood flow regulation via IL-1.

item.title: Nature Communications: Distinct migratory dendritic cell subsets cooperate to prime tissue-resident memory-like CD8⁺ T cells in mouse tumors
item.description: Tissue-resident memory (T RM ) CD8 + T cells in the tumor microenvironment are relevant for anti-tumor immunity and immune checkpoint blockade response. Here, the authors conditionally ablate type 1 and type 2 dendritic cells in a lung cancer mouse model, finding both to be critical for the differentiation and expansion of T RM -like T cells.

item.title: Nature Communications: Genome-wide cross-trait analysis to compare genetic architecture between Parkinson’s disease and kidney-related traits
item.description: Parkinson’s disease has been epidemiologically linked to kidney function, but the extent of their shared genetic basis remains unclear. Here, the authors integrate genome-wide genetic correlation, pleiotropy and colocalisation analyses to identify shared loci and candidate pathways connecting Parkinson’s disease and kidney-related traits.

item.title: Nature Communications: Modular assembly of arterial organoids enables rapid blood perfusion to ameliorate ischemic diseases
item.description: Here, the authors develop injectable arterial organoids that form functional vascular networks in vivo, promoting blood flow restoration and tissue repair in models of ischemic disease by enhancing vascular regeneration.

item.title: Nature Communications: Ociperlimab and tislelizumab in advanced esophageal squamous cell carcinoma (AdvanTIG-203): a phase II study
item.description: PD-1/PD-L1 inhibitors improving survival outcomes in Esophageal Squamous Cell Carcinoma (ESCC) but the survival rates of some subsets ESCC population are still poor. Here this group reports a phase 2 randomized trial evaluating the efficacy and safety of ociperlimab and tislelizumab in patients with PD-L1 TAP ≥ 10%, unresectable, locally advanced, recurrent or metastatic ESCC.

item.title: Nature Communications: Omaveloxolone functions as a molecular crowbar-like degrader of STING to alleviate aging-related inflammation
item.description: Aging-related inflammation can have excessive activation of the STING pathway as some of its features. Here the authors look at the function of Omaveloxolone and show this compound binds to the base of the STING ligand-binding domain and destabilises STING leading to STING K27-linked ubiquitination and proteasomal degradation and show Omaveloxolone reducing aging associated inflammation in aged male mice.

item.title: Nature Communications: Nano-NucleOTAC-mediated Z-DNA transformation disrupts mycobacterium tuberculosis biofilms and activates antibacterial immunity
item.description: Extracellular DNA (eDNA) from tuberculosis can protect bacteria from host immune responses and antibiotics and can contain Z form eDNA which is harder for DNase to hydrolyze. Here the authors use a nanoparticle system to more specifically target eDNA and the Z form and show cleavage of Z-DNA and improvement of immune responses against TB infection in mice.

item.title: Nature Communications: Proximity biotinylation at the host- Shigella interface reveals UFMylation as an antibacterial pathway
item.description: Here, López-Jiménez et al. develop a proximity biotinylation approach to map the host-bacterial interface and show that intracellular Shigella and Salmonella are targeted by UFMylation, a ubiquitin-like system.

item.title: Nature Communications: Ambient, real-time digitization and datafication of glass slide microscopy towards AI-at-the-microscope
item.description: HistoCAM ambiently captures the pathologist’s full, optically sampled microscope view, enabling real-time digital and AI tools while turning routine slide review into process-aware, AI-ready data.

item.title: Nature Communications: Development-inspired approach for the derivation of functional and transplantable salivary gland organoids from human pluripotent stem cells
item.description: Here, they generate salivary gland epithelial progenitors hPSCs by mimicking in vivo salivary gland development. These progenitors self-assemble into salivary gland organoids in vitro and reconstituted both acinar and ductal structures upon orthotopic transplantation in vivo.

item.title: Nature Communications: Transient activation of ciliary CCR2 signaling promotes the initiation of adipogenesis
item.description: Obesity is linked to chronic inflammation and enhanced adipogenesis. Here, the authors show that preadipocytes transiently form CCR2-enriched primary cilia, allowing inflammatory CCL2 to activate ciliary CCR2 and drive ERK-dependent adipogenesis.

item.title: Nature Communications: Cardiopulmonary hospitalization risks from wildfire-specific and non-wildfire PM 2.5 in 20 US states
item.description: Authors found wildfire-specific PM 2.5 showed greater toxicity per unit exposure than non-wildfire PM 2.5 for cardiopulmonary hospitalizations. As wildfire smoke becomes a major and growing source of air pollution, stronger mitigation strategies are needed.

item.title: Nature Communications: Genetic architecture of MRI-derived cervical spinal cord morphology reveals sensory-motor axis and systemic disease associations
item.description: A genome-wide association study of cervical spinal cord morphology using UK Biobank brain MRI data identifies 179 genetic loci shaping spinal cord morphology, revealing its links to systemic health.

item.title: Nature Communications: Automated screening of autism via a pretrained vision-language model in naturalistic caregiver-child interactions
item.description: Here, the authors develop Autism-CLIP, a vision–language model for automated early autism screening using 3-min home videos of toddlers aged 15–24 months.

item.title: Nature Communications: Multimodal data-driven clustering analysis of heart failure patients identifies two distinct patterns of heart failure with preserved ejection fraction: Results from the PACIFIC-PRESERVED study
item.description: Heart failure with preserved ejection fraction is clinically heterogeneous, complicating efforts to identify patients at highest risk. Here, the authors show that integrating proteomics with machine learning reveals two biologically distinct subtypes with different prognoses, including a high-risk inflammatory cardiorenal phenotype.

item.title: Nature Communications: Sero-catalytic and spatial modeling of dengue virus force of infection in Timor-Leste
item.description: Dengue is a public health concern in tropical and subtropical regions. Here, the authors present findings from a national, population-representative serological survey in Timor Leste and identify substantial spatial variation in force of infection.

item.title: Nature Communications: Effectiveness of the oral rotavirus vaccine ROTASIIL among children hospitalized with acute gastroenteritis in India
item.description: Here, using pooled data from two multi-center observational studies, the authors analyze the effectiveness of the ROTASIIL ® vaccine in protecting young children against moderate to severe rotavirus diarrhea, finding that three doses of this vaccine provided good protection, especially among younger children, highlighting the need for timely and complete vaccination.

item.title: Nature Communications: Compound Z247611722 Exhibits Antifungal Activity by Inhibiting Serine Palmitoyltransferase
item.description: This study identifies and characterizes Z247611722, a novel fungicidal compound active against multiple Candida species, and demonstrates that it inhibits sphingolipid biosynthesis by targeting serine palmitoyltransferase.

item.title: Nature Communications: Plasma autoantibody profiling via PhIP-seq and machine learning for diagnosis of esophageal squamous cell carcinoma
item.description: Oesophageal squamous cell carcinoma is often diagnosed in later stages, which limits potential treatment options. Here, the authors develop a PhIP-seq model to diagnose oesophageal squamous cell carcinoma across multiple cohorts.

item.title: Nature Communications: Next-generation functional diagnostic paradigm for musculoskeletal diseases based on live SWIR imaging
item.description: Here, the authors develop a live SWIR imaging strategy to enable dynamic, multi-component functional diagnosis of musculoskeletal diseases. It visualizes synovial fluid flow during locomotion, reveals patellar maltracking, and shows bone and vascular kinematics during healing.

item.title: Nature Communications: Preclinical and clinical investigation of VES001, an oral small molecule sortilin receptor inhibitor for the treatment of frontotemporal dementia: a first-in-human randomized placebo-controlled phase 1 trial
item.description: Treatment for frontotemporal dementia due to GRN haploinsufficiency (FTD-GRN) are lacking. Here, in this preclinical and Phase 1 clinical trial, the authors show that VES001, an oral small molecule sortilin inhibitor, is safe and well tolerated, and increased progranulin levels.

item.title: Nature Communications: Early coconut oil exposure suppresses chronic experimental Crohn’s disease via myristic acid and enhanced regulatory T cells
item.description: Here, the authors show that coconut oil and the fatty acid myristic acid suppress Crohn disease-like intestinal inflammation in mice through multiple mechanisms, supporting a potential role for these dietary fats in promoting protective immune gut responses in Crohn’s disease.

item.title: Nature Communications: Angiotensin II exacerbates intracerebral hemorrhage in mice via heparin-like antithrombin activation and coagulation dysfunction
item.description: Here, the authors show that angiotensin II acts as a key coagulation regulator with heparin-like antithrombin activation function in mediating hemorrhage. Targeting the angiotensin II coagulation pathway could be a novel strategy to mitigate cerebral bleeding events.

item.title: Nature Communications: CpG hypermethylation and WNT/AP-1 cooperativity define the epigenetic landscape and a clinical subgroup of high-risk pediatric adrenocortical carcinoma
item.description: Pediatric adrenocortical tumours (pACTs) are rare and difficult to treat. Here, the authors perform integrated multi-omics analysis of 214 pACTs and identify four distinct risk groups and potential therapeutic targets.

item.title: Nature Communications: Global brain activity links subcortical degeneration to cortical tau progressively across Braak regions over early Alzheimer’s disease stages
item.description: This study finds that reduced infra-slow global brain activity may link degeneration of a key subcortical cholinergic region to progressive cortical tau accumulation in early Alzheimer’s disease.

item.title: Nature Communications: Huntington’s disease vasculopathy is barrier-type-selective and arteriolar-dominant with spatially-coupled astrogliosis and reversible by S1pr1 stimulation
item.description: Here the authors map Huntington’s pathology by barrier and vessel type with two-photon imaging, mass-spec signatures and mouse/human data. They reveal arteriolar susceptibility, spatially matched astrocyte activation and S1pr1 stimulation as potential therapy.

item.title: Nature Communications: PKM2 AP: a micropeptide inhibits vascular calcification via molecular glue-mediated ubiquitination of PKM2
item.description: The study identifies a micropeptide that protects against vascular calcification, a major complication of chronic kidney disease. The micropeptide acts through a molecular glue-like mechanism to promote PKM2 degradation, suppress glycolysis and reduce vascular calcification in mice.

item.title: Nature Communications: Chronic loneliness and isolation phenotypes and physical and mental health in older adults
item.description: Chronic loneliness was associated with poorer physical and mental health, while loneliness onset showed similar but weaker associations. Social isolation primarily affected mental health, while remission may confer cognitive benefits.

item.title: Nature Communications: Structural basis of IgLON5 autoantibody recognition in autoimmune encephalitis
item.description: Anti-IgLON5 disease is a rare neuro-immunological disorder characterized by the production of autoantibodies against the cell adhesion molecule, IgLON5. Here, the authors examine the B cell receptor repertoire of an individual with this condition and present a cryo–electron microscopy structure of a patient-derived antibody clone in complex with IgLON5.

item.title: Nature Communications: LGR5-positive fibroblasts orchestrate skin mechanoadaptation through JAK1 modulation
item.description: Mechanical stress induces LGR5+ fibroblasts that promote adaptive tissue remodeling by limiting fibrosis through JAK1 modulation. The study reveals a conserved mechanism of adaptation to mechanical stress and suggests a strategy for regenerative therapy.

item.title: Nature Communications: In vivo CRISPR screens identify dual functions of DNMT3A in mediating tumor immune evasion
item.description: DNMT3A regulates the anti-tumor activity of CAR-T cells. Here, based on in vivo CRISPR screens, the authors identify tumor cell-intrinsic DNMT3A as a mediator of immune evasion, showing that DNMT3A modulates TNF signalling and cholesterol biosynthesis to impair CD8 T cell anti-tumor immunity.

item.title: Nature Communications: Cardiac fibroblast deletion of PTBP1 modulates the profibrotic response by alternative splicing
item.description: Post-transcriptional regulation of cardiac fibroblast phenotypes during fibrotic cardiac remodeling remains poorly defined. Here, the authors demonstrate that RNA-binding protein PTBP1 regulates alternative splicing to direct the profibrotic response in multiple cardiac injury models.

item.title: Nature Communications: Urban exposures, frailty, and mental illness in World Trade Center Health Program responders
item.description: Higher exposure to long-term air pollution, heat, and less neighborhood greenery is linked to increase in frailty and mental illness test scores among the World Trade Center (WTC) responders. These effects were stronger among those with higher WTC-related exposure histories.

item.title: Nature Communications: Proteasome inhibition alleviates proteinuria in Lmx1b knock-in mice with dysfunctional LIM domains
item.description: Mutations in the LIM domains of LMX1B cause ubiquitin-mediated proteasomal degradation and result in podocyte injury. Inhibition of the proteasome ameliorated renal symptoms in Lmx1b knock-in mice, thus providing proof of principle for a novel therapeutic strategy.

item.title: Nature Communications: Evaluating the consequences of childhood adiposity on the human plasma proteome at four timepoints across the lifecourse
item.description: Childhood obesity can influence health across the lifespan, but its molecular effects at different ages are not fully understood. Here, the authors use lifecourse genetics to show that childhood adiposity alters circulating proteins from childhood into adulthood, identifying potential links to childhood asthma and breast cancer risk.

item.title: Nature Communications: Vascular and lymphatic dysregulation via non-EndoMT Col2a1 signaling in bisphosphonate-related osteonecrosis of the jaw
item.description: Bisphosphonate-related osteonecrosis of the jaw (BRONJ) is a severe complication of antiresorptive therapy with poorly understood vascular mechanisms. Here, the authors identify vascular and lymphatic drivers of BRONJ and show that genetic ablation or silencing of Col2a1 restores endothelial homeostasis and rescues osteonecrotic lesions.

item.title: Nature Communications: Decoding the genomic repertoire of fosfomycin resistance genes in staphylococci
item.description: Here, the authors use 17,000 public genomes to systematically classify and unify nomenclature for fosfomycin resistance genes in Staphylococcus .

item.title: Nature Communications: Fecal microbiota transplantation for the decolonization of mucosal adherent-invasive Escherichia coli in Crohn’s disease: an open-label pilot study
item.description: Here, in a pilot study in humans, the authors provide proof of concept that fecal microbiota transplantation can be used for clearing harmful E. coli from the gut lining of people with Crohn’s disease, highlighting the potential of microbiome-targeted therapies in inflammatory bowel disease.

item.title: Nature Communications: Assessing the use of automatic speech recognition and large language models for individuals with language impairments
item.description: Speech-enabled AI systems may be less reliable for people with language impairments. Here, the authors evaluate ASR-LLM pipelines across aphasia, child language impairment and dementia datasets, identifying transcript errors, repetition, and length as key factors affecting performance.

item.title: Nature Communications: A nested case-control study of air pollution and congenital heart defects via circulating proteins
item.description: Prenatal exposure to air pollution has been linked to risk of congenital heart defects (CHD). Here the authors report that periconception exposure, especially to NO₂, is associated with higher CHD risk and distinct maternal and cord blood protein signatures.

item.title: Nature Communications: Atlas of genetic architecture and exploratory temporal interaction networks of plasma protein-based organ and system aging
item.description: This study provides a comprehensive atlas integrating genetic, environmental, and interactive insights into organ and system aging using multiple plasma protein-based networks, informing future research on targeted anti-aging strategies.

item.title: Nature Communications: A dual-site oral nanovaccine programs anti-colorectal tumor immunity from small intestinal priming to large intestinal boosting
item.description: Here the authors report the design and characterization of a nano-vaccine composed of antigen- and CpG-loaded nanoparticles stabilized by β glucan and plant-derived lipids, showing that, after oral administration, it induces immune priming in the small intestine as well as acts as in situ vaccine to trigger anti-tumor immunity in colorectal cancer.

item.title: Nature Communications: Explainable data generation from observed small samples by matrix tri-factorization
item.description: Here the authors propose an explainable data generation approach called EDG that operates under extreme sample scarcity by exploiting inherent low-dimensional principles contained in the observed high-dimensional data via matrix tri-factorization.

item.title: Nature Communications: Recurrent mechanisms of biallelic epigenetic inactivation reveal new putative tumour suppressor genes in prostate cancer
item.description: Epigenetic biallelic inactivation in prostate cancer remains to be explored. Here, the authors develop a computational method Epi2Hit that integrates the hemizygous genomic disruptions with patterns of hypermethylation at regulatory CpG sites to identify biallelic inactivation in tumour suppressor genes.

item.title: Nature Communications: A core transcriptional regulatory circuitry controls super-enhancer-driven activation of LGR5 in colorectal cancer
item.description: MYC can be transcriptionally regulated by distal super-enhancers (SEs) in cancers. Here, the authors show that MYC, along with ETS2 and FOXP1, form a core regulatory circuit that controls SE-driven transcription in colorectal cancer.

item.title: Nature Communications: Deep learning CT signature for predicting early liver metastases in pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma
item.description: Predicting the risk of early liver micrometastases (ELM) is crucial for identifying patients who are most likely to benefit from neoadjuvant therapy (NAT) in pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) yet most deep learning models focus mainly on primary tumours. Here, the authors show that the non-invasive Mamba based model is able to integrate multi-phase spatiotemporal CT imaging features from both the primary pancreatic tumour and liver regions to predict the risk of ELM in PDAC.

item.title: Nature Communications: CD73 disruption with tumor-specific CRISPR/Cas9 nanoparticles reduces adenosine-mediated immunosuppression and amplifies response to chemotherapy
item.description: Extracellular adenosine, generated by the hydrolysis of ATP by CD39 and CD73, contributes to immunosuppression in the tumor microenvironment (TME). Here the authors report that disruption of CD73 with tumor specific CRISPR/Cas9 nanoparticles reduces adenosine mediated immunosuppression in the TME and amplify response to chemo-immunotherapy.

item.title: Nature Communications: Precision inflammation targeting via myeloperoxidase mediated antioxidant melanin nanomedicines for chronic inflammation therapy
item.description: Chronic inflammation threats health due to unspecific drugs. Here the authors show in hepatopulmonary syndrome and inflammatory bowel disease models, an anti-inflammatory melanin nanomedicine platform that targets inflamed tissues and is mediated by myeloperoxidase.

item.title: Nature Communications: Gut microbiota composition outperforms chronological age in predicting systemic inflammation and incident disease risk
item.description: Here, characterizing 1,199 adults, the authors find that gut bacteria patterns predict inflammation and future disease risk better than age, with an identified microbiota type showing signs of “inflammaging” decades earlier, while a diverse microbiota is linked to better health.

item.title: Nature Communications: Refining biopsy strategies stratified by PI-RADS score in men: a systematic review and network meta-analysis
item.description: Optimal biopsy strategies for lesions with Prostate Imaging Reporting and Data System (PI-RADS) scores of 3-5 remain uncertain. Here, the authors show that for PI-RADS 3–5 lesions, saturation targeted biopsy and ipsilateral systematic biopsy combined with targeted biopsy (ips-SB + TB) exhibit comparable detection rates of clinically significant prostate cancer to systematic plus targeted biopsy (SB + TB), supporting refined biopsy strategies that challenge the necessity of bilateral systematic biopsy. However, targeted biopsy alone remains insufficient, and omitting systematic biopsy in PI-RADS 5 lesions is not supported by current evidence.

item.title: Nature Communications: Embryo selection by non-invasive preimplantation genetic testing for aneuploidy in women of advanced maternal age: a randomized, clinical trial
item.description: Non-invasive preimplantation genetic testing for aneuploidy (niPGT-A) can detect embryo chromosomal aneuploidy by analyzing the cell-free DNA in embryo culture media, but evidence for clinical efficacy is insufficient. Here the authors report a randomised controlled trial involving 1,152 women aged 35–42 years that shows no difference in the primary outcome of ongoing pregnancy rate between the intervention group with niPGT-A and the control group with morphological selection.

item.title: Nature Communications: Arginine metabolism as a mutualistic strategy in the interaction between Porphyromonas gingivalis and Filifactor alocis
item.description: Complex microbial communities are often shaped by cooperation. Here, the authors show that high arginine levels suppress the periodontal pathogen Porphyromonas gingivalis, while Filifactor alocis helps it persist by breaking down arginine, revealing a metabolic partnership.

item.title: Nature Communications: A cytoskeleton-associated Plasmodium protein critical for organelle segregation
item.description: The Plasmodium cytoskeleton is critical for parasite replication. Here, Navarro et al identify and characterise a cytoskeleton-associated protein required for organelle segregation and asexual replication.

item.title: Nature Communications: CNIH4 regulates systemic metabolism and exercise adaptations in male mice primarily through the modulation of β-adrenergic receptor trafficking
item.description: Liu et al. show in male mice that CNIH4 helps adrenaline receptors reach cell surfaces, supporting skeletal muscle glucose use and uphill exercise performance, while promoting brown fat breakdown and heat production in adipose tissue.

item.title: Nature Communications: Puberty, pregnancy, and menopause show shared and distinct structural changes across the lifespan
item.description: Brain volumes decline during puberty and pregnancy, with both shared and distinct regional patterns, while menopause appears to briefly pause rather than speed up ongoing volume loss, as shown by this neuroimaging study directly comparing these three transitions.

item.title: Nature Communications: Canakinumab with chemoradiation and durvalumab consolidation in unresectable stage III non-small cell lung cancer: the phase I/II CHORUS trial
item.description: IL-1β targeting may attenuate myeloid-suppressive pathways and support antitumor immunity. Here, the authors report a phase I/II trial of concurrent canakinumab, an anti-IL-1β antibody, with chemoradiotherapy, followed by consolidation canakinumab plus the anti-PD-L1 antibody durvalumab, in patients with unresectable stage III non-small cell lung cancer.

item.title: Nature Communications: Tislelizumab plus lenvatinib in advanced fumarate hydratase-deficient renal cell carcinoma: a single-arm, phase 2 trial with metabolic biomarker analysis
item.description: Effective first-line treatments for fumarate hydratase-deficient renal cell carcinoma remain poorly defined, despite promising activity of immune checkpoint inhibitor– based combinations. There these authors report efficacy outcomes of a phase 2 clinical trial on tislelizumab plus lenvatinib in fumarate hydratase-deficient renal cell carcinoma patients.

item.title: Nature Communications: A multitask framework for automated multi-frame right upper quadrant ultrasound interpretation and clinical decision support
item.description: Authors developed an AI system for interpreting multi-frame right upper quadrant ultrasound examinations. Across three institutions, it classified findings, generated reports, and predicted the need for cholecystectomy.

item.title: Nature Communications: CBX4 stabilizes NEUROD1 through SUMO-ubiquitin crosstalk to delay β-cell senescence
item.description: As pancreatic β-cells age, CBX4 levels fall. Restoring CBX4 stabilizes the transcription factor NEUROD1 via SUMOylation and phase separation, counteracting its degradation to rejuvenate β-cell function and offering a new diabetes treatment avenue.

item.title: Nature Communications: Dysregulated tissue immunity in human fatal asthma
item.description: Immune mechanisms driving severe asthma and fatal outcomes remain elusive. Through cross-tissue immune profiling of organ donors who died of fatal asthma versus other causes, the authors here reveal mucosal immune dysregulation marked by enhanced T- and B-cell memory, reduced Tregs, and increased lung Th2 and Th1 effectors linked to priming in gut-associated lymph nodes.

item.title: Nature Communications: Neoadjuvant PD1 plus CTLA-4 immune checkpoint blockade in surgically resectable recurrent glioblastoma: a randomized surgical window-of-opportunity trial
item.description: Here the authors report clinical and immunological outcomes of a randomized surgical window-of-opportunity trial designed to test whether dual immune checkpoint blockade targeting PD-1 and CTLA-4 could overcome the adaptive immune resistance previously reported with single-agent anti-PD-1 therapy in patients with surgically resectable recurrent glioblastoma.

item.title: Nature Communications: Helicobacter pylori triggers gastric mucosal remodeling toward a fetal-like transcriptional program via stromal IL-1β signaling
item.description: During tissue homeostasis, gastric epithelial maintenance is governed by Wnt and BMP signaling, whereas injury induces a YAP-driven fetal-like regenerative program. Here, Beccaceci et al. show that H. pylori infection reprograms the gastric mucosa toward a fetal-like state through BMP deficiency and IL-1β-dependent immune-stromal-epithelial crosstalk.

item.title: Nature Communications: System-wide investments generate health and enhance HIV, TB and malaria control in Malawi
item.description: A modelling study of Malawi’s health system shows that combining health system strengthening with disease-targeted programmes delivers twice the return on investment and three times the health impact of disease-focused investment alone.

item.title: Nature Communications: Cadonilimab plus lenvatinib in advanced endometrial cancer: the multicenter single-arm phase II CLEAR-EC trial
item.description: Immune checkpoint blockade has emerged as a therapeutic option for patients with endometrial cancer. Here the authors report the results of a phase II trial of cadonilimab (a bispecific antibody targeting PD-1 and CTLA-4) combined with lenvatinib in advanced endometrial cancer.

item.title: Nature Communications: Phylogenetic analysis of the 2025 Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo
item.description: The study reports the emergence of a new Ebola variant in a remote area of Kasai Province, DR Congo. The findings highlight the need for rapid detection and sequencing to better identify variants and quickly respond to outbreaks.

item.title: Nature Communications: Multiple local PfDHFR I164L haplotype expansions drive Plasmodium falciparum antifolate resistance in Uganda
item.description: PfDHFR haplotypes involving I164L are known to strongly influence antifolate resistance in Plasmodium falciparum. In this study, Asua and colleagues examine the frequency of antifolate-resistance conferring mutations in over 4,700 parasite samples collected in Uganda over a 6-year period. They report that markers conferring antifolate resistance during this time, which may impact chemotherapeutic strategies that are reliant on sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine (SP).

item.title: Nature Communications: First-line tislelizumab plus chemotherapy versus placebo plus chemotherapy in unresectable advanced/metastatic esophageal squamous cell carcinoma: minimum 3-year survival follow-up of a randomized phase 3 trial (RATIONALE-306)
item.description: The RATIONALE-306 trial demonstrated improved overall survival in participants with advanced/metastatic esophageal squamous cell carcinoma treated with tislelizumab plus chemotherapy comparing with those who received placebo plus chemotherapy. Here they report its exploratory long-term efficacy/safety/quality of life analysis after 36.0 months follow-up.

item.title: Nature Communications: Extracellular vesicle proteins monitor and interfere with CLDN18.2-targeted CAR-T cell and antibody therapies against gastrointestinal cancers
item.description: CLDN18.2-targeted CART and antibody therapies are promising for gastrointestinal cancers, but predictive biomarkers and strategies to enhance efficacy are needed. Here, these authors investigate how extracellular vesicle (EV)- derived proteins influence therapeutic response to CLDN18.2-based CAR-T and targeted therapies.

item.title: Nature Communications: Microbial-derived tryptophan metabolites in the infant gut associate with increased risk of asthma following cesarean section
item.description: Here, in the Canadian birth cohort (CHILD), the authors associate 1-year C-section-microbiome with higher asthma risk at age 5, as previously reported in the Danish birth cohort (COPSAC2010), and identify microbial-derived tryptophan metabolites at 1 year of age to mediate the association between C-section and asthma risk.

item.title: Nature Communications: A spatial and temporal transcriptomic atlas of mouse intestinal regeneration in the jejunum
item.description: The intestinal epithelium efficiently regenerates after injury, yet the dynamics underlying this process are not fully understood. Here, the authors use spatial transcriptomics to map the mouse intestine over time after radiation injury, revealing shifts in villus zonation, spatially restricted interferon signaling, altered stem cell populations and a surge in gene transcription that may help fuel recovery.

item.title: Nature Communications: The urinary pathobiont Actinobaculum massiliense can generate androgens via the dirAB pathway
item.description: Urinary bacteria linked to prostate cancer are often overlooked. Here, the authors developed a high-throughput assay to identify androgen-producing urinary microbes, isolated key bacterial strains, and discovered genes and enzymes that enable steroid conversion, revealing mechanisms by which urinary bacteria may influence host hormone biology.

item.title: Nature Communications: Motifs of brain cortical folding from birth to adulthood
item.description: Guo and colleagues parse cortical folding variability into a family of distinct anatomical motifs that generalise across adults and neonates. These motifs shed light on structural asymmetry, heritability, and folding-function links.

item.title: Nature Communications: Functional annotation of insulin-responsive genes in human adipocytes reveals PLCXD1 as a lipid storage regulator
item.description: Frendo-Cumbo et al. combine transcriptomics with functional screening in adipocytes to identify PLCXD1 as an insulin-regulated gene. This atypical phospholipase is localized to early endosomes and promotes lipid storage in human fat cells.

item.title: Nature Communications: A fully integrated sample-to-answer diagnostic platform enables rapid quantification of post-transplant infection at the point-of-care
item.description: Opportunistic infections are among the leading causes of graft loss for organ transplant recipients. Here authors introduce a protein-free CRISPR-like assay platform called MONITOR, which, when combined with pre-amplification, achieves single-molecule sensitivity, enabling sample-in-answer-out quantification of post-transplant infections in resource-limited settings.

item.title: Nature Communications: Gene regulatory network analysis identifies auranofin as an anti-atherosclerotic drug
item.description: Gene regulatory networks (GRNs) are powerful platforms to unravel the genetic complexity of coronary artery disease (CAD). Here, the authors show that a GRN-based drug repurposing coupled with pre-clinical and clinical validation uncovers auranofin as a new potential CAD therapy.

item.title: Nature Communications: RAGE mediates LPS-induced inflammatory pain in human skin – a double-blind, randomised, placebo-controlled full crossover study
item.description: Bacterial lipopolysaccharide induces inflammation. Inflammatory pain is a major clinical challenge lacking suitable and viable human pain models. Here the authors present a double-blind, randomised, placebo controlled full crossover clinical trial examining the pain response to LPS challenge in human skin and suggest a role for RAGE in the LPS-induced inflammatory pain response.

item.title: Nature Communications: Trifluoroacetate mediated reduction of atherosclerosis in mice
item.description: Trifluoroacetate (TFA), long assumed to be an inert peptide counterion, is a bioactive modulator of PPARα signaling that induces peroxisome proliferation, alters lipid metabolism, and attenuates atherosclerosis in mice.

item.title: Nature Communications: Sex- and fiber type-specific remodeling of the muscle proteome implicates CSRP3 in resistance training-induced hypertrophy
item.description: Here, the authors show that changes in the muscle fiber proteome following 8 weeks of resistance training are both sex- and fiber type-specific. This includes greater upregulation of CSRP3 in type II than type I fibers, which in mice was shown to be involved in muscle growth.

item.title: Nature Communications: Subtyping metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease using electronic health record-linked genomic cohorts reveals diverse etiologies and progression
item.description: From multi-year Mayo Clinic records on liver disease, researchers identified five distinct patient patterns. The method for generating liver disease subtypes is robust, producing transferable subtypes across diverse patient cohorts.
